library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2022_dabigatran"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fcvm.2022.998751>

Liu 2022 developed a population PK model for total dabigatran after oral
dabigatran etexilate from rich data in 118 healthy Chinese volunteers, linked
it sequentially to three coagulation biomarkers -- activated partial
thromboplastin time (aPTT), prothrombin time (PT) and anti-factor IIa
(anti-FIIa) activity -- and then refitted the PD layer to the pooled healthy
volunteer and patient data (167 Chinese adults with non-valvular atrial
fibrillation) with the PK held fixed. Table 2 of the paper reports both fits,
so two models are packaged:

* `Liu_2022_dabigatran` -- the final **integrated** model (Table 2,
  "Integrated model" columns), with creatinine clearance and age effects on
  the PD parameters.
* `Liu_2022_dabigatran_healthy` -- the **healthy-volunteer** PK/PD model
  (Table 2, "Healthy volunteers model" columns), whose PD has no covariates.

Both share the same structure: a two-compartment PK model with first-order
absorption and a fixed absorption lag, age and HDL-cholesterol effects on
apparent clearance, and a direct linear effect of the plasma concentration on
each biomarker (Equation 5, `PD = E0 + K * Cc`).

```{r models}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Liu_2022_dabigatran"))
mod_hv <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Liu_2022_dabigatran_healthy"))
```

# Population

The healthy volunteers (n = 118; 85 men, 33 women) were aged 18-41 years
(median 22), weighed 50.3-73.8 kg (median 60.3) and had a median Cockcroft-Gault
creatinine clearance (CrCL) of 120.18 mL/min (86.96-171.02) and a median
HDL cholesterol of 1.42 mmol/L. Each received one 150 mg dabigatran etexilate
capsule (Pradaxa reference period of a four-period bioequivalence crossover),
fasted (n = 59) or after a high-fat meal (n = 59), with 17-18 PK samples and
PD samples at 0, 2, 8 and 12 h.

The patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (n = 167; 104 men, 63
women) were aged 39-91 years (median 73), weighed 44-115 kg (median 70) and had
a median CrCL of 64.48 mL/min (23.00-179.55) and HDL cholesterol of 1.04 mmol/L.
They took 110 mg twice daily at steady state and contributed PD samples at
trough (more than 10 h post-dose) and peak (2 h post-dose); 23 of them also
gave sparse PK samples that were used only for external validation of the
healthy-volunteer PK model (Liu 2022 Table 1 and Methods).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Liu_2022_dabigatran")()$population`.

Every value below is from Liu 2022 Table 2 unless noted. "HV" is the

| PK structure | two-compartment, first-order absorption with lag | same | Results "PopPK model"; Supplementary Figure 1 |
| IIV model | exponential, `theta_i = theta_tv * exp(eta_i)` | same | Methods Equation 1 |
| PD model | `PD = E0 + K * X1`, X1 = plasma concentration | same | Methods Equation 5 |
| Covariate model | `theta_tv * (COVref / COV)^theta_cov` | same | Methods Equation 3, reinterpreted (see below) |

# Assumptions and deviations

## Covariate equation

Methods Equation 3 is printed as
`theta_i = theta_tv * exp(eta_i) * theta_cov^(COV_i / COV_pop)`. Taken
literally, a subject at the median covariate value would not have the typical
value: the median healthy volunteer would have
CL/F = 166 x 0.694 x 0.506 = 58 L/h. A 75-year-old would then have
CL/F = 166 x 0.506^(75/22) x 0.694 = 11 L/h. The packaged models instead use the
power form `theta_tv * (COV_ref / COV_i)^theta_cov`, with the healthy-volunteer
medians (age 22 years, HDL 1.42 mmol/L, CrCL 120.18 mL/min, Table 1) as
references. Two of the paper's own simulations support this form.

**PK (Discussion).** For a 75-year-old taking 150 mg twice daily, the paper
reports a median simulated concentration of 48.68 ng/mL at 12 h (trough) and
168.22 ng/mL at 14 h (peak). HDL is not stated and is taken at its reference
value. The chunk below gives the typical-value prediction under the three
candidate forms.

```{r covariate-form-pk}
dosing_bid <- function(n_dose = 2, amt = 150) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 12 * (seq_len(n_dose) - 1), evid = 1L, amt = amt,
             cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
}
obs_rows <- function(times) {
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_,
             dvid = 1L)
}
ev_disc <- bind_rows(dosing_bid(), obs_rows(c(12, 14))) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
  mutate(AGE = 75, HDLC = 1.42, CRCL = 30)

# Typical-value solve: individual-level CL computed outside the model for the
# alternative forms, injected by overriding lcl with the age factor folded in.
cl_forms <- c(
  "(22 / AGE)^0.506 (packaged)" = 166 * (22 / 75)^0.506,
  "(AGE / 22)^0.506" = 166 * (75 / 22)^0.506,
  "0.506^(AGE / 22) x 0.694 (Equation 3 as printed)" = 166 * 0.506^(75 / 22) * 0.694
)
disc <- lapply(names(cl_forms), function(nm) {
  m <- rxode2::ini(mod, lcl = log(cl_forms[[nm]]), e_age_cl = 0, e_hdlc_cl = 0)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev_disc, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
                                     useLinCmt = FALSE))
  data.frame(form = nm, `CL/F (L/h)` = round(cl_forms[[nm]], 1),
             `C 12 h (ng/mL)` = round(s$Cc[s$time == 12], 1),
             `C 14 h (ng/mL)` = round(s$Cc[s$time == 14], 1),
             check.names = FALSE)
}) |> bind_rows()
disc <- bind_rows(disc, data.frame(form = "Liu 2022 Discussion (reported median)",
                                   `CL/F (L/h)` = NA, `C 12 h (ng/mL)` = 48.68,
                                   `C 14 h (ng/mL)` = 168.22, check.names = FALSE))
knitr::kable(disc)
```

Only the `(22 / AGE)^0.506` form reproduces the paper's numbers. It is within
2% of both, while the other two forms are off by a factor of two or more.

```{r covariate-form-pk-check}
stopifnot(
  abs(disc$`C 12 h (ng/mL)`[1] / 48.68 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(disc$`C 14 h (ng/mL)`[1] / 168.22 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

**PD (Results, "Exposure simulation").** The paper simulates a "typical
patient" on 150 mg and patients with CrCL 50 mL/min (150 mg) and 30 mL/min
(110 mg). It reports the 2 h peak and the trough. The troughs are at 0.05 h,
before the first dose has been absorbed, so they equal the baselines; PT and
anti-FIIa troughs are identical across the three scenarios. Because the
covariate and dose effects are multiplicative, the ratio of each scenario's
drug-induced increment (peak minus trough) to the typical patient's increment
isolates the CrCL term. The packaged form predicts these ratios as
`(120.18 / CrCL)^theta_cov` times the dose ratio. The aPTT baseline ratio is
`(120.18 / CrCL)^0.252`.

```{r covariate-form-pd}
paper_pd <- tribble(
  ~scenario,          ~crcl,  ~dose, ~marker,     ~peak,  ~trough,
  "typical, 150 mg",  120.18, 150,   "aPTT",      40.20,  32.49,
  "typical, 150 mg",  120.18, 150,   "PT",        13.01,  11.79,
  "typical, 150 mg",  120.18, 150,   "antiFIIa",  130.58, 20.13,
  "CrCL 50, 150 mg",  50,     150,   "aPTT",      48.13,  40.42,
  "CrCL 50, 150 mg",  50,     150,   "PT",        18.97,  11.79,
  "CrCL 50, 150 mg",  50,     150,   "antiFIIa",  377.68, 20.13,
  "CrCL 30, 110 mg",  30,     110,   "aPTT",      51.58,  45.98,
  "CrCL 30, 110 mg",  30,     110,   "PT",        26.59,  11.79,
  "CrCL 30, 110 mg",  30,     110,   "antiFIIa",  543.18, 20.13
)
theta_crcl <- c(aPTT = 0, PT = 2.02, antiFIIa = 1.35)
ratio_chk <- paper_pd |>
  group_by(marker) |>
  mutate(
    paper_ratio = (peak - trough) / (peak[1] - trough[1]),
    model_ratio = (dose / 150) * (120.18 / crcl)^theta_crcl[marker]
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(scenario != "typical, 150 mg")
base_chk <- paper_pd |>
  filter(marker == "aPTT") |>
  mutate(paper_ratio = trough / trough[1], model_ratio = (120.18 / crcl)^0.252) |>
  filter(scenario != "typical, 150 mg")
bind_rows(
  ratio_chk |> mutate(quantity = paste(marker, "peak increment")),
  base_chk |> mutate(quantity = "aPTT baseline (trough)")
) |>
  select(scenario, quantity, paper_ratio, model_ratio) |>
  mutate(across(c(paper_ratio, model_ratio), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         `% diff` = round(100 * (model_ratio / paper_ratio - 1), 1)) |>
  rename(Scenario = scenario, Quantity = quantity,
         `Ratio to typical (paper)` = paper_ratio,
         `Ratio to typical (model)` = model_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

All the PT, anti-FIIa and aPTT-baseline ratios agree within about 5%. The
direction confirms the Discussion's statement that "CrCL negatively affects the
slope". With the printed `2.02` read as a positive power of `CrCL / 120.18`,
the slope would fall rather than rise as renal function declines. The aPTT peak
increment has no CrCL effect on K1 and only scales with dose: it is 7.71 s for
both the typical patient and CrCL 50 at 150 mg. At CrCL 30 on 110 mg it is
5.60 s, which matches 7.71 x 110/150 = 5.65 s. No CrCL term on K1 is therefore
consistent with Table 2.

```{r covariate-form-pd-check}
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ratio_chk$model_ratio[ratio_chk$marker != "aPTT"] /
            ratio_chk$paper_ratio[ratio_chk$marker != "aPTT"] - 1) < 0.08),
  all(abs(ratio_chk$model_ratio[ratio_chk$marker == "aPTT"] /
            ratio_chk$paper_ratio[ratio_chk$marker == "aPTT"] - 1) < 0.05),
  all(abs(base_chk$model_ratio / base_chk$paper_ratio - 1) < 0.05)
)
```

The direction of the HDL effect cannot be checked the same way, because no
reported simulation varies HDL. It is encoded with the same
`(reference / covariate)^theta` convention that the age and CrCL effects
demonstrably follow, so higher HDL lowers CL/F. The age effect on the aPTT
baseline also follows that convention, with the healthy-volunteer median age
of 22 years as reference. The paper does not say which median it used for the
pooled integrated fit. Using 120.18 mL/min for CrCL is the value the
simulation ratios recover.

## Variance scale of IIV and residual error

The Table 2 "IIV" column is read as NONMEM omega^2 (variance of the
log-normal eta), and the residual-error rows as sigma^2 (variance of the
additive error). The paper's text quotes 0.0144 as "1.44%" and 30.1 as "30.1 s".
Read as standard deviations, the residual values would be implausible: an
additive SD of 30.1 s on an aPTT baseline of about 30 s, or 643 ng/mL on an
anti-FIIa activity of about 100 ng/mL. The paper describes all of them as
"relatively low". The variance reading also reproduces the paper's simulated
means and confidence-interval widths better than a CV reading; see the
"Biomarker peaks and troughs" section below.

## Other decisions

* **CL/F IIV in the integrated model.** The integrated-model IIV cell for
  CL/F is a dash, while V2/F keeps its healthy-volunteer IIV of 1.14. The
  paper states that the PK model was not modified in the integrated fit, so
  the healthy-volunteer CL/F IIV (0.142) is carried forward and held constant.
* **aPTT residual error in the integrated model.** The integrated cell
  prints `0.0258 (17%)`, which is the same value and RSE as the aPTT E0 IIV
  directly above it and is taken as a typesetting duplicate. The
  healthy-volunteer value (variance 30.1, SD 5.49 s) is carried forward.
* **Anti-FIIa baseline.** Methods say "E0 for anti-FIIa activity fixed 0",
  but Table 2 reports an estimated E2 (14.9 and 20.5 ng/mL, with RSEs). The
  table values are used.
* **Slope units.** Table 2 and the text give the slopes in "s.mL.ug-1".
  They are applied per ng/mL of dabigatran, the unit in which the
  concentration is measured. Per ug/mL, the drug effect on aPTT would be about
  0.01 s and invisible, which contradicts the paper's simulated peaks.
* **Residual error of the PK model.** Equation 2 describes a combined
  proportional and additive model, but Table 2 and the text report only an
  additive error (221). Only the additive term is encoded.
* **Lag time.** It is held constant at 0.634 h; the paper took the value
  "from the literature" without a citation in Table 2.
* **Food effect.** Fed versus fasted dosing was screened but not retained,
  so it does not appear in either model.

# Healthy-volunteer PK: single 150 mg dose

A virtual cohort of 118 healthy volunteers is simulated with the
healthy-volunteer model. Age and HDL are drawn from log-normal distributions
centred on the Table 1 medians and truncated to the observed ranges; the
paper gives no dispersion beyond the range.

```{r hv-cohort}
set.seed(2022)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2022)
n_hv <- 118
rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, med, sdlog, lo, hi) {
  x <- rlnorm(n * 4, log(med), sdlog)
  x <- x[x >= lo & x <= hi]
  x[seq_len(n)]
}
cov_hv <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_hv),
  AGE = rtrunc_lnorm(n_hv, 22, 0.2, 18, 41),
  HDLC = rtrunc_lnorm(n_hv, 1.42, 0.2, 1.02, 2.5),
  CRCL = 120.18
)
t_obs <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12,
           16, 24, 36, 48, 72)
ev_hv <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n_hv), time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 150, cmt = "depot",
             dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_hv), time = t_obs) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  left_join(cov_hv, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  mutate(treatment = "150 mg single dose")
sim_hv <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hv, ev_hv, keep = "treatment",
                          useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r hv-vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated total dabigatran after a single 150 mg dose in healthy volunteers (median and 90% prediction interval of the individual predictions); cf. Liu 2022 Supplementary Figure 3A."}
sim_hv |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Total dabigatran (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## NCA of the simulated healthy volunteers

```{r hv-nca}
conc_hv <- sim_hv |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_hv <- ev_hv |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_hv, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_hv, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
)
nca_hv <- PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data)
summary(nca_hv)
```

The paper reports no NCA for this cohort, so there is no reference table. As
an internal check, the median AUC0-inf should be close to dose / (CL/F) at
the median covariates: 150 mg / 166 L/h = 904 ng*h/mL.

```{r hv-nca-check}
auc_med <- median(nca_hv$result$PPORRES[nca_hv$result$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"],
                  na.rm = TRUE)
auc_med
stopifnot(abs(auc_med / (150 / 166 * 1000) - 1) < 0.15)
```

## Steady-state check against the Discussion simulation

The paper's Discussion reports median simulated concentrations of
48.68 ng/mL at 12 h and 168.22 ng/mL at 14 h for 75-year-old patients on
150 mg twice daily. A cohort of 200 such patients is simulated with the
integrated model, with HDL at its reference value, since the paper does not
state it. The concentrations at 12 h and 14 h are taken as `clast.obs` over the
intervals 0-12 h and 12-14 h.

```{r disc-nca}
n_pt <- 200
t_pt <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.5), 14)))
ev_pt <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_pt), time = c(0, 12)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 150, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_pt), time = t_pt) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(AGE = 75, HDLC = 1.42, CRCL = 30, treatment = "150 mg BID, age 75") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_pt <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pt, keep = "treatment", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_pt <- sim_pt |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_pt <- ev_pt |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, treatment)
nca_pt <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_pt, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_pt, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = c(0, 12), end = c(12, 14), clast.obs = TRUE)
))
ref_pt <- data.frame(treatment = "150 mg BID, age 75", end = c(12, 14),
                     clast.obs = c(48.68, 168.22))
tbl_pt <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_pt, ref_pt, by = c("treatment", "end"),
  units = c(clast.obs = "ng/mL")
)
tbl_pt |>
  rename(`Sampling time (h)` = end) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r disc-nca-check}
sim_med <- nca_pt$result |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "clast.obs") |>
  group_by(end) |>
  summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(abs(sim_med$med / c(48.68, 168.22) - 1) < 0.10))
```

# Biomarker peaks and troughs (Results, "Exposure simulation")

Each scenario below has the same 200 virtual patients (identical random
effects, so the scenarios differ only in CrCL and dose). The paper reports means and 95%
confidence intervals from 1,000 replicates, at 2 h (peak) and 0.05 h (trough)
after the first dose. Age and HDL are held at the reference values, which the
reproduced typical-patient trough of aPTT indicates.

```{r pd-sim}
scen <- tribble(
  ~scenario,          ~CRCL,  ~amt,
  "typical, 150 mg",  120.18, 150,
  "CrCL 50, 150 mg",  50,     150,
  "CrCL 30, 110 mg",  30,     110
)
sim_pd <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen)), function(i) {
  ev_i <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = seq_len(n_pt), time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = scen$amt[i],
               cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n_pt), time = c(0.05, seq(0.5, 12, by = 0.5))) |>
      mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    mutate(CRCL = scen$CRCL[i], AGE = 22, HDLC = 1.42) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
  # Same seed and event layout in every scenario -> identical eta draws.
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(20221028)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_i, useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(scenario = scen$scenario[i])
}) |>
  bind_rows()

pd_sum <- sim_pd |>
  filter(time %in% c(0.05, 2)) |>
  select(scenario, time, aPTT, PT, antiFIIa) |>
  pivot_longer(c(aPTT, PT, antiFIIa), names_to = "marker") |>
  group_by(scenario, marker, time) |>
  summarise(sim_mean = mean(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(what = ifelse(time == 2, "peak", "trough")) |>
  select(-time) |>
  left_join(
    paper_pd |>
      pivot_longer(c(peak, trough), names_to = "what", values_to = "paper"),
    by = c("scenario", "marker", "what")
  ) |>
  mutate(`% diff` = round(100 * (sim_mean / paper - 1), 1),
         sim_mean = signif(sim_mean, 4))
pd_sum |>
  arrange(match(scenario, scen$scenario), marker, what) |>
  select(scenario, marker, what, paper, sim_mean, `% diff`) |>
  rename(Scenario = scenario, Marker = marker, Statistic = what,
         `Liu 2022 (mean)` = paper, `Simulated (mean)` = sim_mean) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The troughs reproduce the baselines, and the peaks are within about 10% of the
paper's means.
For the typical patient, the paper's reported 95% CI for the anti-FIIa peak is
120.40-140.77 ng/mL. The slope IIV of PT (omega^2 1.25) and anti-FIIa
(omega^2 1.1) is heavy-tailed, so the mean of 200 subjects moves by roughly
10% between random draws. That level is set by the typical-patient row, and
the CrCL scenarios then follow from the deterministic ratios checked above.
The aPTT peak is the least well reproduced, at about 4% low. The paper notes
that its aPTT simulation was the least accurate of the three biomarkers
("poorer simulation accuracy than for PT and anti-FIIa activity", Discussion).

```{r pd-sim-check}
# Baselines carry no drug and no CrCL-dependent IIV for PT / anti-FIIa:
# the trough means equal the Table 2 baselines.
tr <- pd_sum |> filter(what == "trough")
stopifnot(abs(median(tr$`% diff`)) < 5)
# Peaks: centre of the nine peak comparisons. The slope IIV is heavy-tailed,
# so individual stochastic means are not asserted.
pk <- pd_sum |> filter(what == "peak")
stopifnot(abs(median(pk$`% diff`)) < 15)
```

```{r pd-fig, fig.cap = "Simulated biomarker time courses after the first dose for the three scenarios (median of the individual predictions); cf. Liu 2022 Figure 5."}
sim_pd |>
  select(scenario, time, aPTT, PT, antiFIIa) |>
  pivot_longer(c(aPTT, PT, antiFIIa), names_to = "marker") |>
  group_by(scenario, marker, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(value), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, med, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~marker, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Median prediction", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Healthy-volunteer versus integrated PD

The healthy-volunteer PD model (no covariates) and the integrated model at the
healthy-volunteer reference covariates differ only through their re-estimated
baselines and slopes. The typical-value comparison after a single 150 mg dose
is below.

```{r hv-vs-int}
ev_one <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 150, cmt = "depot",
             dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 2, 8, 12), evid = 0L, amt = 0,
             cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
) |>
  mutate(AGE = 22, HDLC = 1.42, CRCL = 120.18) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))
tv <- function(m, lab) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev_one, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
                                useLinCmt = FALSE)) |>
    select(time, Cc, aPTT, PT, antiFIIa) |>
    mutate(model = lab)
}
bind_rows(tv(mod_hv, "healthy volunteers"), tv(mod, "integrated")) |>
  mutate(across(c(Cc, aPTT, PT, antiFIIa), \(x) signif(x, 4))) |>
  rename(`Time (h)` = time, `Cc (ng/mL)` = Cc, `aPTT (s)` = aPTT,
         `PT (s)` = PT, `anti-FIIa (ng/mL)` = antiFIIa, Model = model) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
